idea.en: Describe the structures seen in the mid oesophageal two chamber view

label.en: From the four chamber plane the sector rotates forward until the right heart drops out and the left atrial appendage appears

note.en: What you see: From the four chamber plane the sector rotates forward until the right heart drops out and the left heart fills the image. The left ventricle and left atrium stack vertically with the mitral valve between them, showing the anterior and inferior walls of the ventricle. The left atrial appendage appears as a finger like pouch at the edge of the atrium and the left upper pulmonary vein enters nearby. This plane profiles the inferior wall well, so regional wall motion of that territory is judged here.

label.en: Left ventricle cavity, left atrium cavity, anterior and posterior leaflets of the mitral valve

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Left ventricle cavity, left atrium cavity, anterior and posterior leaflets of the mitral valve, left atrial appendage, left upper pulmonary vein, oesophagus behind the left atrium.

steps.en: What you see: From the four chamber plane the sector rotates forward until the right heart drops out and the left heart fills the image. The left ventricle and left atrium stack vertically with the mitral valve between them, showing the anterior and inferior walls of the ventricle. The left atrial appendage appears as a finger like pouch at the edge of the atrium and the left upper pulmonary vein enters nearby. This plane profiles the inferior wall well, so regional wall motion of that territory is judged here.

Landmarks to confirm: Left ventricle cavity, left atrium cavity, anterior and posterior leaflets of the mitral valve, left atrial appendage, left upper pulmonary vein, oesophagus behind the left atrium.

Common mistakes and correction: Stopping rotation short of 90 degrees so the aorta lingers in view: continue rotating until the appendage appears. Sitting too low in the oesophagus so the appendage never shows: withdraw slightly. Foreshortened anterior wall from too much anteflexion: relax flexion and re centre the apex.

Normal values with units: Probe depth about 30 cm from the incisors. Multiplane angle near 90 degrees. In health the inferior and anterior walls thicken symmetrically and the appendage empties with each beat. Left ventricular ejection fraction 52 percent or above in men and 54 percent or above in women marks the lower reference limit.

Pitfalls: Rheumatic heart disease is common in India, so commissural fusion and leaflet tip thickening seen in this plane should be recorded and quantified with Doppler. Spontaneous contrast in an enlarged atrium can mimic thrombus, so gain and focus should be optimised before calling clot. A prominent appendage ridge can mimic a mass to the unwary.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: Start from a good mid oesophageal four chamber at about 30 cm from the incisors. Rotate the multiplane forward toward 90 degrees while watching the right heart fade and the left atrial appendage come into view. Keep the mitral valve centred and the apex inside the sector. Fine tune a few degrees either side of 90 degrees to open the ventricle to its longest length. If the aorta appears, the rotation has stopped short, so continue toward 90 degrees.

q.en: From the four chamber plane, how is the two chamber plane reached?

why.en: The two chamber plane sits near 90 degrees of multiplane rotation from the four chamber baseline.

q.en: Which finger like pouch at the atrial edge confirms the two chamber plane?

why.en: The left atrial appendage appears at the atrial edge in the two chamber plane.

q.en: The aorta still shows in the image. What should you do?

o.en: Continue rotating until the appendage appears
Freeze and label it left ventricle
Turn on colour over the whole sector

why.en: A lingering aorta means rotation stopped short of 90 degrees, so continue rotating.
